# The Data

```{r}
#| label: preliminaries
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# load packages
library(tidyverse) 
library(knitr)
library(gtsummary)
library(ggstatsplot)
library(downlit)
library(broom)
library(here)
```

```{r}
#| label: data
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# load the data
df <- read_csv(here("Data", "data-results-kyla.csv"))

df <- df |>
  select(
    Status,
    Agreement
  )
```


## The Relationship Between Students Status and Their Perception of NVSU's No Monday Class Schedule Implementation

The Data set is gathered from 68 students with 2 variable. 

- `Status` Regular, Iregular.

- `Agreement` Agree, Disagree.

This Data aims to determine the relationship between students' status and their perceptions of NVSU's No Monday Class Schedule, particularly its effects on their academic workload, time management, study habits, personal well-being, and overall student experience.

The first 6 rows of the Agreement data set are shown in @tbl-Agreement.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-Agreement
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| tbl-cap: "The first 6 observations of the data set."

df |>
  head() |> # getting the first six rows of the data
  kable(col.names = c("Learning Agreement", "Learning Status")) # creating a table

```

## Descriptive Statistics

The frequency distribution of students' perceptions of the No Monday Class Schedule implementation when grouped according to their academic status is presented in the summary table. It shows how students from different year levels and academic programs perceive the new schedule. The data will identify the majority of students who agree or disagree with the implementation, particularly in terms of academic workload, time management, study habits, and personal well-being. This will provide an overview of students' opinions and experiences regarding the new scheduling policy at Nueva Vizcaya State University.


```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary statistics of `Status` when grouped according to `Agreement`."
#| message: false

df |> 
  tbl_summary(
    by = Agreement,
    include = Status
  )
```
```{r}
df|>
 tbl_cross(
 row = Status,
 col = Agreement,
 percent = "column",
 margin = c("row","column"),
 label = list(
 Status ~ "Learning Status",
 Agreement ~ "Learning Agreement"
)
)
```
# Hypothesis Testing

## Research Question

Is there a Difference in Students Agreement with having no Monday classes among different Academic Status.

## Hypothesis and Test Statistics

- $H_0:p_{Agreement}-p_{Status}=0$; Students Status does not Affects the Agreement .

- $H_a:p_{Agreement}-p_{Status}\ne0$; Students Status Affects the Agreement.

- Significance level, $\alpha=5\%\,\text{or p-value}\,\le\.05$.

- **Pearson's** $\chi^2$-test of independence

- Independence.

- Expected counts: all expected counts are $\gt5$ (see @tbl-expected).

```{r}
# Create contingency table
observed <- table(df$Agreement, df$Status)

# Perform chi-squared test
chi_test <- chisq.test(observed)

# Extract the expected counts
expected <- chi_test$expected

# View expected counts
expected |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    " " = c("Agree", "Disagree")
  ) |>
  relocate(" ", .before = 1) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2))) |>
  kable()


```
## Results and Interpretation

The bar chart and test statistics are shown on @fig-test.

```{r}
#| label: fig-test
#| fig-cap: Bar chart and test statistics.
#| fig-height: 3

ggbarstats(
  data = df,
  x = Agreement,
  y = Status,
  bf.message = FALSE,
  legend.title = "Agreement"
)
```

> The bar chart shows that all Irregular passengers disagreed, whereas most Regular passengers (76%) agreed. A Chi‑squared test showed a significant relationship between passenger status and agreement (\(p < .001\)). Because the *p*-value is less than 0.05, we reject the null hypothesis. There is strong evidence that Irregular and Regular passengers differ significantly in their agreement levels.
